title: Loose == juggling: "0" == false and (PHP7) 0 == "SAVE10" silently void a valid coupon
sourceContent:
<?php
// discount.php - apply a coupon, with loose-comparison traps
function applyCoupon($subtotal, $couponCode) {
    // TRAP: if $couponCode is the string "0", ("0" == false) is TRUE,
    // so a legitimate coupon "0" is treated as "no coupon".
    if ($couponCode == false) {
        return $subtotal;
    }
    // TRAP: in PHP 7, (0 == "SAVE10") is TRUE; PHP 8 fixed it.
    if ($couponCode == 0) {
        return $subtotal;
    }
    $rate = ($couponCode === "SAVE10") ? 0.10 : 0.0;
    return $subtotal - ($subtotal * $rate);
}
notes: PHP loose == juggles types: "0" == false is true, and pre-PHP-8 0 == "SAVE10" is true (string coerced to int 0), so ANY non-numeric coupon voids the discount. PHP 8 changed the 0 == "abc" case to false, so the result is version-sensitive. The Java/.NET target must use an explicit typed comparison (=== semantics), not a naive == translation.
